newsitem.title: LEBANON: Pro-Israeli chief blasts Lebanon death sentence.
newsitem.headline: Pro-Israeli chief blasts Lebanon death sentence.

text.p: The head of Israel's client militia in south Lebanon, General Antoine Lahd, said foreign powers were responsible for Lebanese authorities passing a death sentence against him.

"The tasks of the impotent and weak-willed Lebanese state are apparently limited to implementing the behests of those foreign parties who have the power to make decisions about Lebanon," Lahd was quoted as saying in Beirut newspapers on Wednesday.
This was apparently in reference to Syria, whose 35,000 troops across Lebanon make it the country's main power broker.

Last Friday, a Beirut military court passed a death sentence in absentia after convicting Lahd of treason for collaborating with Israel, with which Lebanon is officially at war. He commands the 3,000-strong South Lebanon Army which helps Israeli troops occupy a south Lebanon border zone.

"The Lebanese state's recent sentence against me is merely an attempt to give Lebanese citizens the false impression that it is working hard to liberate the border area, although it knows very well that by behaving in this manner it puts a great distance between itself and this objective," he added.
